title: Vice Trophy Guide — Grand Theft Auto VI (PS5)

trophies.guide: The platinum unlocks itself once the other 54 trophies are earned, so there is no separate task to do for it. Treat it as the finish line of the roadmap: story first, then strangers and side missions, then collectibles and activities, and finally the cleanup counts. It pops the moment the last of the 54 lands.

Official trophy list — PlayStation, via PSNProfiles

The platinum unlocks automatically when the last one pops.

trophies.guide: Reach 100% in the game's own completion checklist. That checklist is broader than the trophies: it counts story, side missions, activities and collectibles together, so work through the roadmap stages in order and use the in-game stats screen to see what is still missing. Expect this to be one of the last two trophies, alongside the platinum itself.

trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, drifts and other driving feats the game counts as stunts. The count builds up naturally across normal play, so do not grind it early: keep playing, and check the tracker count late in the game. If it is short near the end, chain stunt jumps on open roads to close the gap. The count of 250 is the one the official description states.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity in the game at least once — racing, fishing, the shooting range, bowling, arcade games, drone races and whatever other activity types the world offers. The official description does not list the types, so use the in-game activities menu as the checklist: one try of each type is enough, no win is required. Confirm the full type list post-release.

Work through the range's challenge list one weapon or drill at a time, repeating a challenge until the gold threshold is met. This is a skill grind, not a story task, so leave it for the activities stage and take it in short sessions.

Learn the fishing mechanics first in free fishing, then take the challenge when you can land catches consistently. trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose it and escape. The partner must be present for it to count, so start this during a mission or activity you do together. Once at 4 stars, break line of sight, hide, and wait for the wanted level to clear — do not get caught or killed. It can be retried, so a failed escape costs nothing but time.

trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops one after another without losing your wanted level — the wanted level must stay active across all three robberies. Plan a route of three close shops, move fast between them, and keep the police at bay without letting the wanted level drop. If the level clears or you are caught, start the chain again. The count of 3 is the one the official description states.

Trigger Combat Focus only when at least five enemies are visible, and chain the takedowns before it ends. It can be retried freely, so keep attempting it in busy fights.

Steal or borrow a plane on the airfield and take off. It is flagged missable because it is a single-moment stunt at one location; in practice it should be repeatable in free roam, so confirm post-release whether it can be retried any time.

If you are spotted, the attempt fails — abort and try again, since detection is the only condition. It is flagged missable because a single spotted run can spoil the attempt, though the robbery itself can be retried.

trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties — 8 garages, as the tracked count on PSNProfiles and Exophase lists it. Garages are bought with in-game money, so save up during the money stage and buy them one by one as they become affordable. Owning them also gives you somewhere to keep the vehicles the discovery trophy needs.

trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. As you discover vehicles for the discovery trophy, register them in the app — ten registrations is all it takes. The count of 10 is the one the official description states.
